name: Drift
editorial_article: "Drift" is a landmark 2018–2019 experimental project by the British electronic pioneers Underworld, encompassing a massive, year-long series of audio, visual, and literary releases. Rather than adhering to the traditional album-tour cycle, Karl Hyde and Rick Smith committed to a "foolhardy" schedule of releasing new music and accompanying videos on a weekly basis, aiming to capture an instinctive and immediate creative energy. The project effectively disrupted the band's standard production workflow, replacing the safety of three-year cycles with a relentless weekly deadline that forced the duo into a state of continuous, unfiltered output.\n\nThe resulting work is a sprawling, multifaceted archive of electronic music that shifts effortlessly between ambient textures, experimental jazz-fusion, and driving techno. Collaborations were central to this process, featuring an eclectic array of artists such as the Australian avant-garde group The Necks, producer Ø [Phase], and members of the post-punk band Black Country, New Road. The title itself serves as both a nod to drift racing culture—reflecting the spontaneous, high-velocity nature of the production—and a literal description of the project’s fluid evolution, as tracks were released, remixed, and re-contextualized across five massive "Episodes" and the eventual "Drift Series 1" box set. By documenting their process in real-time, Underworld transformed the act of creation into a public performance, prioritizing honesty and artistic challenge over polished, predictable studio perfection. The project stands as a testament to the band’s enduring curiosity and their ability to reinvent their own sonic landscape after decades at the forefront of global electronic culture.
